summary.headline: Spandana returned to profit in Q4 FY26 with PAT of INR5 crore, ending six loss-making quarters, as AUM grew 12% QoQ to INR4,420 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 marked the first quarterly profit after six quarters, with PAT of INR5 crore versus a loss of INR95 crore in Q3 and PBT of INR8 crore versus a loss of INR125 crore. AUM rose 12% QoQ to INR4,420 crore, the first AUM increase after eight quarters, with disbursements up to about INR500 crore per month from INR400 crore in Q3. Opex fell to about INR161 crore from INR195 crore, and PPOP rose to INR39 crore from INR8 crore. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 3.8% (4.2% in Dec-25), NNPA at 0.73% and X-bucket collection efficiency at 99.7%. NIM contracted to 9.9% from 11.1% as borrowing costs stayed high.

segments.name: Spandana core MFI (JLG and individual)
segments.commentary: Disbursements averaged about INR500 crore per month in Q4 versus INR400 crore in Q3 and INR300 crore in Q2. About 80% of AUM is now under the new BRE and guardrails, with 99.7% X-bucket collection efficiency. Customer base is a little over 11.5 lakh, with 1.2 lakh new borrowers added in Q4 versus about 63,000 in Q3.

segments.name: Criss Financial (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Micro-LAP book is about INR322 crore, with GNPA at about 1.2%. The individual loan book is about INR260 crore, and GNPA fell to 6.5% from 11.45% after one ARC transaction and better collections.

guidance_outlook: Cost of borrowings expected at about 12.5% blended in FY27, below 12.5% for the full year per CFO; no large escalation expected.
Disbursements to hold at about INR500 crore per month for three to four months, then rise to INR550-600 crore per month.
AUM targeted at about INR6,500 crore by March 2027, with management reiterating the figure when pressed.
Management indicated INR9,000-10,000 crore AUM by FY28 is still a fair assessment, implying about 40-45% annual growth.
No formal profitability guidance; management aims to stay profitable for FY27.
Yield expected to move up toward the disbursement yield of about 25.25% during FY27 from 22.8% now.
Medium-term opex target of 7-8% of AUM; near-term aim to bring quarterly opex down from INR160 crore.
Target to add about 7 lakh new borrowers in FY27, taking the base from 1.1 million to about 1.6 million.
Customer satisfaction score target of 95%, up from 71% currently, by end of Q1 FY27 or shortly after.
CFL merger process started; expected to take 5-6 months.
Migration to Perfios LOS: individual loan product expected by end of Q1 FY27 or early Q2; JLG migration around October-November 2026.
capex_capacity: Branch network is about 1,250 branches; management says the head office is sized for about INR12,500 crore of AUM without new fixed cost, with frontline headcount to be added as volumes grow.
Frontline loan officer additions are needed to scale beyond about INR8,000 crore AUM.
Individual loan pilot to launch in June or July 2026 in selected Spandana branches; Criss Financial to source once milestones are met.
New LOS platform being built by Perfios, with the first product (individual loans) targeted for end of Q1 FY27 or early Q2.
demand_pricing: Lender overlap (Spandana plus three) at about 4.8%; 34% of borrowers are Spandana-only, 37% Spandana plus one, and 25% Spandana plus two.
Rejection rates at 60-65%, down from 70-80% about two quarters earlier; management expects this to persist for a while.
Sourcing mix in Q4: about 45% new customers, of which about 10% new-to-credit and 35% new-to-Spandana.
Average ticket size about INR60,000; new-to-credit about INR50,000-60,000; existing and new-to-Spandana rising to about INR60,000-85,000.
Loan pricing 23-26% depending on vintage; individual loans also priced at 23-26%.
Average EMI has risen to about INR1,800-2,000 from INR400-500, per management, which weakens group guarantee support.
Digital repayment average about 22%; management is seeking an industry target of about 50%.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost of funds and yield move in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects blended cost of borrowings around 12.5% and below 12.5% for the full year. Yield is 22.8% currently against a disbursement yield of about 25.25%, and should move closer to that during FY27.

qa_highlights.question: When will the customer base return to growth and how many new borrowers will be added?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1.2 lakh new borrowers were added in Q4 versus about 63,000 in Q3. The FY27 goal is 7 lakh new borrowers, taking the base to about 1.6 million from 1.1 million.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 AUM and profitability expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects AUM of about INR6,500 crore by March 2027 with disbursements of INR500 crore per month rising to INR550-600 crore. No profit guidance is given, but the aim is to stay in the black.

qa_highlights.question: What controls explain the 99%+ collection efficiency on new book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company applies stricter rules than the SRO guardrails: it does not lend to customers 30+ days past due on the disbursal date, and 98% of Q4 disbursals were to regular customers. Next-day outreach to missed instalments is now a daily process.

qa_highlights.question: How will the individual loan product be controlled given the opex cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Individual loans are unsecured, at INR1-4 lakh tickets, 23-26% pricing, and a 24-month average tenor (up to 3-4 years). Management said it stays profitable at 99.5% collection efficiency, and it will be offered to business owners with an enterprise for working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Criss Financial book stabilising?
qa_highlights.answer: Criss Financial GNPA fell to 6.5% from 11.45% after one ARC transaction and better collections. Management expects further decline as the new underwriting book seasons.

risks_watch: Liquidity tightness could push borrowing costs above the 12.5% guided level; NIM fell to 9.9% from 11.1%.
Seasonal stress from El Nino and fertiliser-related issues could hit rural collections; management says it is tightening sourcing and focusing on X-bucket and 1+ bucket collections.
Criss Financial GNPA at 6.5% and the individual loan pilot both need to show performance.
Profitability depends on the 99.5% collection efficiency target, with credit costs of about 2.5-3% if 50% of flows are recovered.
Individual loan product sits outside SRO oversight, which raises underwriting and discipline questions.
Achieving 40-45% AUM growth needs sustained sourcing given 60-65% rejection rates and high attrition in frontline staff.
Perfios LOS migration timelines (individual loan by June-July 2026; JLG around October-November) and CFL merger timeline (5-6 months).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the turnaround, with the CEO and CFO stressing the profit return, collection efficiency and CSAT gains. Cautious on the macro, the El Nino and fertiliser seasonality, and on borrowing costs. Management was reluctant to give profit guidance and deferred on the individual loan product's scale.
key_quotes: We managed to disburse around INR 500 crores a month during the last quarter, which was up against the INR400 crores per month that we used to disburse in Q3.
So, overall for the year, we believe it should be, below 12.5%.
Any level of growth, I can't compromise on collection efficiency, especially in the X-bucket. It has to be 99.5%.
Opex up to INR8,000 crores in terms of some people in the frontline I may have to add.
